title: Exact Total Stretches
statement: A shop records its daily profit (which may be negative). Return how many stretches of consecutive days add up exactly to k.

answerKey.pattern: Running (prefix) sums with a hash map of how often each sum appeared
keyPoints: Keep the running total of profits
A stretch ending today sums to k when an earlier running total equals running - k
Add how many times running - k has appeared, using a map from running total to count
Start the map with 0 seen once
edgeCases: Negative values (a sliding window does not work)
The map must start with {0: 1} for stretches that start on day one
acceptableSlowerApproaches: Try every start and end with a running sum: O(n^2)

hints: Checking every start and end is O(n^2). What does the sum of days i to j equal in terms of running totals?
sum(i..j) = running(j) - running(i - 1). You need earlier running totals equal to running(j) - k.
Count earlier running totals in a map, and start it with 0 seen once.
